_read_me: Defaults. Don't edit this file — copy any key you want to change into ~/.claude/chat-weight/config.json (all your projects) or <project>/.claude/chat-weight.json (one project). Those win over this file.
_weight_why: Chat weight = how much the chat has grown since its first reply, against the point where starting fresh is cheaper. That point is restart_multiple x the restart cost (what a fresh chat must re-load to carry on, learned from your own fresh chats; restart_tokens_default until there are 3 of them), but never past memory_cap_pct of the model's memory. The bar reads fresh_chat_pct there.
_statusline_empty_why: The empty square in the terminal's bottom bar. Many terminal fonts draw ⬜ small and hollow; 🔳 always comes from the emoji font, so it matches the coloured squares. Set it back to ⬜ if your terminal draws that one well.
_updates_why: Once a day chat-weight downloads one small public file (VERSION) from its GitHub page, in the background, to see if a newer version is out. If one is, Claude says so once per chat; nothing updates until you say "update chat-weight". Nothing about you is sent: it is a plain download, like opening a web page. Set check_for_updates to false to stop the check.
_paths_why: Both paths are relative to the project folder (the nearest one holding .git or .claude). "../" steps out of it, so a sub-project can share its parent's notes and rules.
_windows_why: How much each model can hold, by model-id prefix, used only for the memory_cap_pct limit. The status line reads the real number from Claude Code and that wins; this table is the fallback (the desktop app has no status line). Longest matching prefix wins, so a model released after this file (say claude-opus-7) falls under its family line and needs no update.

middle.for: building a plan that is already agreed

small.for: routine: renaming, moving files, docs, running tests

models._add_a_tool: To add another tool, add a line like  "Codex": {"top": "<model>", "middle": "<model>", "small": "<model>"}  and update "checked". Names in a tool without names_stay_current get '(or newer)' added once 'checked' is over 90 days old.
